newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-IMPRESSIVE HINGIS WINS TEEN BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-IMPRESSIVE HINGIS WINS TEEN BATTLE.

text.p: Martina Hingis enjoyed the rare pleasure of beating a player younger than herself when she crushed Anna Kournikova in straight sets to reach the fourth round at the French Open on Saturday.

The much-awaited battle of teenagers between the 16-year-old Hingis and Russian Kournikova, who is only 15, turned out to be a one-sided fight with the Swiss world number one winning 6-1 6-3 in just 42 minutes.

Hingis, who struggled in the previous round when she was stretched to three sets by Italian Gloria Pizzichini, was back to her brilliant best, leaving Kournikova helpless with an impressive display of smart tennis.
"I needed that match two days ago (against Pizzichini), which was not very easy for me," said Hingis. "I felt much better today and I'm very happy with the way I played."
Kournikova, who is only allowed to play a limited number of tournaments because she is not yet 16, said she needed time before matching opponents like Hingis.

"She's got more experience than I have and that showed today," she said. "I was a bit nervous because it's my first French Open and it was my first match on centre court but I did play better towards the end."
Kournikova and Hingis had not met since the second round at the US Open in the junior ranks three years ago when the Russian left in tears after losing 6-0 6-0.
Hingis, who has yet to drop a match this year, seems to have fully recovered after a riding accident last month which left her out of action for six weeks with an injured knee.
"I try to spend as little time on court as I can but physically, I'm okay," she said. "I felt pretty strong today."
Hingis, who ousted German Steffi Graf from the number one spot in March, delighted the crowd with her mix of powerful baseline strokes, clever drop shots and sharp volleys.

"I don't often beat younger players," she said. "But it's good to meet players like Anna or Venus (Williams) because they play differently from the older players and I'll probably have to face them quite often in the future."
Hingis will have little time to rest as she will play 16th seed Barbara Paulus of Austria on Sunday for a place in the quarter-finals.
"It's very hard to beat her but if you do, you get a lot of bonus points," said Paulus.
When asked if she felt confident, Paulus remained silent for a few seconds before saying "yes" in a low voice.

Hingis, who said before the tournament that she was expecting little, is slowly realising she could go far. She even decided to turn down an invitation to go riding next week with Olympic equestrian champion Pierre Durand of France.
"I have enough of my own problems, I play another match tomorrow," she said. "There are no days off to go horse riding."
